clue.text: Dismiss Parisian from law officer's team, lacking heart

parts.note: de is the French word for 'from', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: lacking its heart means the central letter of the team word goes

parts.note: a posse is the band a sheriff gathers

explanation.surface: A French person is thrown off a sheriff's posse for being faint-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' drops the middle S of POSSE, leaving POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to dismiss or remove them from office.

clue.text: Ventured to admit time was flying

indicators.note: to admit means to let something inside, so the time letter goes within

parts.note: dared means ventured, took the risk

explanation.surface: Someone risked conceding that time was passing quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time was flying' looks like one idiom; 'was flying' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Darted and was flying both describe moving very swiftly, as a synonym pair.

clue.text: First-class mail should have this now!

definitions.text: First-class mail should have this now!

parts.words: First-class mail should have this now!
parts.note: split 4,5 it is the mail plus the speed first-class letters are meant to travel at; whole, it means immediately

explanation.surface: A grumble that premium letters ought to arrive quickly these days.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is mail plus speed; the whole word is the adverb meaning 'at once', echoed by 'now!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, immediately, as urgent letters were once marked to travel.

clue.text: Wallflower becoming less wild, lacking nitrogen

parts.note: shrinking means getting smaller, becoming less

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the nitrogen letter is removed

parts.note: violent means wild, uncontrolled
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A garden plant fades and grows tamer for want of nitrogen fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallflower' sounds like a plant in this gardening picture, but it means a shy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a timid person who hangs back at parties, the same as a shy, retiring type.

clue.text: Staff, unusual weapon clutched by maiden queen

indicators.note: clutched by means held inside the other letters

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: unusual tells us the word weapon is rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange weapon is gripped by a maiden queen, perhaps Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden queen' tempts as one figure, the Virgin Queen; it is two abbreviations either side of the scrambled weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff and manpower both mean the workforce available to an organisation.

clue.text: Skilled aviator goes over river as some land

indicators.note: goes over here means covers, so the pilot letters wrap round the river letter

parts.note: an ace is a fighter pilot with many kills

explanation.surface: An expert pilot flies across a river and above some fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' sounds like flying overhead; it means the ace surrounds R.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area, a measured plot of ground.

clue.text: What one may resort to when there's no point in solving

definitions.text: What one may resort to when there's no point in solving

parts.words: What one may resort to when there's no point in solving
parts.note: 'no point' means a blunt pencil, not a futile crossword

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to do when solving a puzzle feels pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No point' looks like despair at a crossword; it is a blunt pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil sharpener is the device you use to restore a blunt lead.

clue.text: Oddly rejected, oddly evil, we will head north and flourish

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, from bottom to top
odd letters thrown out, so only the even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: Wicked people, cast out, threaten to march north and thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly rejected' keeps DLEIW, the even letters of 'oddly evil, we'; 'head north' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a sword is to flourish it, brandishing it in the hand.

clue.text: Kept cool

definitions.meaning: set aside or held back, like a booked table

explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means both held back for someone and emotionally restrained, distant.

clue.text: Beads twisted or perhaps about right

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so or is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the letters for perhaps go around the right letter

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps

explanation.surface: Beads are tangled, or roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of prayer beads used by Catholics.

clue.text: Royal family member, this one's brother's son

parts.note: the brother of this royal lady is a prince, and the 's gives a further S

explanation.surface: A royal relative is identified as the son of this person's brother, a nephew.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to the answer itself: her brother is a PRINCE, his 's adds S, and son adds another S.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, the daughter of a monarch.

clue.text: Rest should contribute half of table tip servers raised

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
contribute signals letters given from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Waiters should share half of the table's tip, raised as a fair cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Rest should contribute half' as the definition; only 'Rest' defines, and 'should contribute half of' signals the hidden letters, which 'raised' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break, a period of rest or relief.

clue.text: Liquid he canned and improved

indicators.note: liquid means flowing, not fixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man tinned some liquid and made it better.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhanced and improved both mean made better in quality, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Revolutionary communist, idiot that could ignite something

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: red is the usual label for a communist
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A radical red, foolish enough to light a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as a political label for the communist; it reverses RED and NIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is dry kindling material used to catch a spark and start a fire.

clue.text: Flirted, messed about!

indicators.note: messed about means jumbled, so the letters of flirted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flirted and fooled around, toying with affections.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with someone is to flirt and toy with their feelings without seriousness.

clue.text: What the setter could offer for Poles? It leads to disaster

parts.words: What the setter could offer for Poles
parts.note: read as wordplay, slippery is an anagram signal and slope is fodder whose letters rearrange to poles

explanation.surface: A setter wonders how to clue Poles, then warns of a route to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer as a clue would be 'slippery' (anagram signal) plus SLOPE, giving POLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery slope is a course of action that leads step by step to ruin.

clue.text: Leotard's divertingly worn by male artist

indicators.note: worn by means the male letter goes inside, wrapped by the leotard letters
divertingly means turned aside from its course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer's leotard is worn amusingly by a man who is an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' puts M inside OLDASTER, an anagram of LEOTARDS from 'divertingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter from before about 1800, so an artist.

clue.text: One writing lines, say, is twiddling pens

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as a pen holds animals, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A schoolchild writing lines idly twiddles their pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing tools; it means encloses, hiding the answer in 'lineS, SAY, IS Twiddling'. 'lines' tempts as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is a writer of essays, someone who composes prose pieces.

clue.text: Magic vehicle carrying Santa to France with bit of help

parts.note: Father Christmas rides in a sleigh
F is the international vehicle code for France
a hand is a bit of help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A magical vehicle takes Father Christmas to France, with a little assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is conjuring trickery, the dexterity a magician uses.

clue.text: In France she is in training, being a little round

indicators.note: is in means placed inside, so the French pronoun goes within the training letters

parts.note: PT is physical training
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A French woman in training becomes a bit plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little round' sounds like plump; it is a noun, a small ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small round ball, as of shot or compressed matter.

clue.text: Get drinkers' club to welcome non-drinker in

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the club letters surround the abstainer

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a fellowship for problem drinkers
TT is teetotal, a non-drinker
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinkers' club is urged to admit a teetotaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinkers' club' seems a pub; AA is the support group.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to get or achieve it, a synonym.

clue.text: Young man with charisma rising and rising, then falling

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: lad is a boy or young man
it means sex appeal, charisma

explanation.surface: A charismatic young man rises and rises, then falls from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'rising' reverses LADIT; 'rising, then falling' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal water ebbs and flows, going up and then down with the tide.

clue.text: Aircraft witness simply reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the result is how the phrase sounds

parts.note: see means witness and plain means simply, together said as one

explanation.surface: An observer gives a plain account of seeing an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaplane is an aeroplane that takes off from and lands on water.

clue.text: Free party for peacekeepers?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, which sends peacekeepers
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration for UN soldiers that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free party' tempts as no-charge; 'Free' is the verb to release.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or bond is to free or loosen it.

clue.text: Slow arrangement for Elton after horrible din

indicators.note: after puts the Elton letters behind those from din
horrible here signals that din is twisted out of shape
an arrangement of a piece reworks it, so the letters of Elton are reordered

explanation.surface: A slow musical arrangement for Elton John follows an awful racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks musical, but it is the signal to reorder the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means lazy, sluggish, slow to act.

clue.text: Impress trendy whisky-maker no end

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a still is apparatus for distilling whisky

explanation.surface: A fashionable whisky distiller makes an endless impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to impress it gradually on someone's mind.

clue.text: Elton rocks, hosting the broadcast TV event

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elton John rocks out while hosting a televised charity show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' scrambles both words, and 'hosting' means the singer's letters hold the other three.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long televised fundraising programme, a broadcast charity event.

clue.text: Monotonous hill — turned back, as something dangerous in wood

parts.note: dry means dull, monotonous

indicators.note: turned back means reversed, read the other way

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A dull hill-walker turns back, sensing danger in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something dangerous in wood' is a fungus, not a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that destroys timber in buildings.
